title: Pimiento Chili (Pimiento F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Pimiento chili is an F1 hybrid chili variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Pimiento chili is an F1 hybrid chili variety, also sold or known as Pimiento F1 or Pimiento panigang pepper. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical (Condor brand).

heroImage.alt: A farmer watering vegetable beds in Pulilan, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Pimiento chili is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Pimiento F1 or Pimiento panigang pepper, this is the same chili. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [chili variety finder](/crop-varieties/chili), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first harvest about 53 days after transplanting. Yield, by the seller's count: 30 to 35 t/ha (company figure), about 141 fruits a plant. No trial on record checks these figures yet, so treat them as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit chili fields most often: [tomato leaf curl](/diseases/tomato-leaf-curl), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest about 53 days after transplanting.
**Yield:** 30 to 35 t/ha (company figure), about 141 fruits a plant.
**Fruit:** Panigang (siling haba) type, straight and uniform, glossy dark green with firm, thick flesh, about 11.6 cm long and 8.1 g.
A strong, spreading plant that matures early.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a new panigang (siling haba) hybrid in Allied Botanical's line. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual chili on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Pimiento chili

Decide first between siling haba, the long green finger chili for cooking, and siling labuyo, the small hot one. Hybrids bear more and for longer, while open pollinated labuyo keeps its heat and lets you save seed. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: Is Pimiento F1 the same as Pimiento?
items.a: Yes. Pimiento F1 is another name for Pimiento. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Pimiento?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
